title: Standing OpenTelemetry demo on AWS EKS shipping to ClickStack on ClickHouse Cloud
context: The laptop workshop in observability-workshop/ runs the upstream OpenTelemetry demo on microk8s inside a Multipass/OrbStack guest and ships traces, logs, metrics and session replay to a managed ClickStack service on ClickHouse Cloud. It is tied to one Mac. This plan builds a NEW sibling repo, otel-demo-eks/ (at /Users/barretta/workspace/ch/202609-offsite-workshop/otel-demo-eks, created by task 1 with `git init -b main`), that stands the same demo up on AWS EKS in ~5-8 minutes and scales it to zero when idle. The full design, with every user decision and verified upstream fact, is in .claude/plans/i-d-like-to-transform-sprightly-quail.md — read it before implementing any task. Decisions already made by the user (do not re-open): OpenTofu for IaC; region us-east-1; IAM Identity Center (SSO) profile auth; keep the EKS control plane and scale the managed node group to 0 when idle (~$73/mo standing cost); nightly EventBridge Scheduler scale-to-zero via universal target (no Lambda); session replay kept, so the patched frontend image is built once with docker buildx and pushed to ECR; PRIVATE access via kubectl port-forward only (no LoadBalancer/Ingress/NodePort); ClickHouse Cloud is open to any IP so nodes sit in public subnets with no NAT gateway; Graviton (arm64) nodes so the frontend image builds natively on Apple Silicon. Pinned versions (verified 2026-09-09): demo chart open-telemetry/opentelemetry-demo 0.41.0; terraform-aws-modules/eks ~> 21.25 (needs hashicorp/aws >= 6.59); terraform-aws-modules/vpc ~> 6.7; EKS Kubernetes 1.36; clickhouse/clickstack-otel-collector 2.38.0; demo source commit d6fd782e (the session-replay patch is generated against it). Host tooling already present: aws CLI 2.36, OpenTofu 1.12, Docker 29 + buildx (native linux/arm64), kubectl 1.37, helm 4.2.4, jq. NOT present: shellcheck, eksctl, terraform. REPO ROOT for waves 2+ (worktrees, verification command) is otel-demo-eks/, not the parent directory holding this plan. Wave 1 (task 1) is a single-task inline wave that creates that repo; the orchestrator must cd into otel-demo-eks/ before running the verification command. Tasks 1-6 are file-authoring tasks verified without AWS credentials or cluster access (public registry/chart downloads allowed); only task 7 touches AWS, inline, with the user present for SSO login and approvals, and it commits a sanitized evidence record (LIVE-VALIDATION.md) that the evaluator grades.
constraints: No LoadBalancer, Ingress, or NodePort resources or Helm values anywhere — the storefront is reached only through kubectl port-forward (user decision)
No NAT gateway, private subnets, or VPC endpoints in the OpenTofu config — public subnets only, map_public_ip_on_launch true (user decision)

No credentials, tokens, account ids, or account-specific values (ECR URL, bucket name) committed to the repo — they come from gitignored envvars.* files, `--from-env-file`/`--from-literal` at deploy time, or tofu outputs at run time

No task other than task 1 modifies demo.sh, scripts/check.sh, or any file under scripts/lib/ — later tasks consume that interface; a missing helper is reported in the HANDOFF, not patched in — Amended 2026-09-09 at the deferred-items review with user approval: remediation tasks def-d7 and def-d8 may modify scripts/check.sh and scripts/lib/{common,aws}.sh for exactly the helpers their acceptance criteria name; every other def- task still only consumes the lib interface.

Tasks 1-6 make no AWS API calls, run no tofu apply/plan against a backend, and reach no cluster. Their verification may access the public OpenTofu registry and the OpenTelemetry Helm repository to download pinned providers, modules, and chart 0.41.0, but must not require AWS credentials or cluster connectivity. Only task 7 touches AWS, inline with the user present The def- remediation tasks added 2026-09-09 are under the same offline rule: no AWS API calls, no tofu plan/apply against a backend, no cluster access.

tasks.title: OpenTofu: public-subnet VPC, EKS 1.36 cluster, Graviton node group (min 0), ECR repo, nightly scale-to-zero schedule

acceptance_criteria.text: `tofu -chdir=tofu fmt -check` reports no changes and `tofu -chdir=tofu init -backend=false -input=false && tofu -chdir=tofu validate` succeeds; tofu/.terraform.lock.hcl is committed

tasks.title: Kubernetes files (static demo values, ClickStack collector) plus deploy, tunnel and build-frontend scripts
tasks.why: This is the workshop's telemetry wiring carried over to a cluster with no VM layer: the values file must become static and committable, and the frontend image must come from ECR instead of the guest's containerd.

acceptance_criteria.text: k8s/demo-values.yaml contains no `__` placeholder tokens and: sets jaeger, prometheus, grafana, opensearch enabled: false; keeps the product-catalog and checkout 128Mi memory limits; declares NO service type or nodePort under components.frontend-proxy; under components.frontend sets imageOverride.pullPolicy: Always and an envOverrides list containing only PUBLIC_HYPERDX_ENABLED="true" (no PUBLIC_OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT); under opentelemetry-collector sets extraEnvsFrom to a secretRef named clickstack-otlp-token and config.exporters.otlphttp/clickstack with endpoint http://clickstack-otel-collector.clickstack.svc.cluster.local:4318, headers.authorization "${env:OTLP_AUTH_TOKEN}", retry_on_failure enabled and sending_queue enabled with batch, and service.pipelines traces/metrics/logs exporters lists that include otlphttp/clickstack (traces also debug and span_metrics; metrics and logs also debug)

`helm template otel-demo open-telemetry/opentelemetry-demo --version 0.41.0 -f k8s/demo-values.yaml --set components.frontend.imageOverride.repository=example/frontend --set components.frontend.imageOverride.tag=check` renders successfully and the output contains a frontend Deployment whose container image is exactly `example/frontend:check`, a collector ConfigMap containing the literal `${env:OTLP_AUTH_TOKEN}`, a collector DaemonSet with an envFrom secretRef named clickstack-otlp-token, no Service of type NodePort or LoadBalancer, and no Jaeger, Prometheus, Grafana or OpenSearch workloads

scripts/deploy.sh, in order: aws_login; kubeconfig; load_clickhouse_env; dies with 'run ./demo.sh up' if ng_desired is 0; creates namespaces clickstack and otel-demo via `kubectl create ns ... --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -`; creates Secret clickstack/clickstack-credentials via `kubectl -n clickstack create secret generic clickstack-credentials --from-env-file=envvars.clickhouse --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -`; applies k8s/clickstack-collector.yaml, waits `rollout status deploy/clickstack-otel-collector --timeout=300s` and prints its last 40 log lines; creates Secret otel-demo/clickstack-otlp-token with --from-literal=OTLP_AUTH_TOKEN="$OTLP_AUTH_TOKEN" the same dry-run|apply way; computes TAG=$(frontend_tag) and runs scripts/build-frontend.sh when `aws ecr describe-images --repository-name otel-demo-frontend --image-ids imageTag=$TAG` fails; runs `helm upgrade --install otel-demo open-telemetry/opentelemetry-demo --version "$CHART_VERSION" -n otel-demo -f k8s/demo-values.yaml --set components.frontend.imageOverride.repository="$(tf_out ecr_repository_url)" --set components.frontend.imageOverride.tag="$TAG" --wait --timeout 20m` (adding/updating the helm repo first); calls tunnel_start; prints http://localhost:8080, http://localhost:8080/feature/ and http://localhost:8080/loadgen/. It never writes a file containing secret values to disk

scripts/tunnel.sh with no argument stops any running tunnel then calls tunnel_start; `stop` calls tunnel_stop; `status` calls tunnel_status and exits with its code; anything else prints usage and exits 1

scripts/build-frontend.sh: reads ECR_REPO_URL, ECR_REGISTRY, NODE_PLATFORM, AWS_REGION from tf_out after aws_login; implements ensure_demo_checkout ported from observability-workshop/scripts/08-build-frontend.sh (DEMO_DIR default opentelemetry-demo, overridable by env; blobless `git clone --no-checkout --filter=blob:none` of https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-demo.git then `git checkout --detach $DEMO_REF`; `git apply --check` then `git apply` of $SDK_PATCH; an existing checkout whose src/frontend/package.json lacks @hyperdx/browser gets the patch applied); computes TAG=$(frontend_tag); unless --force, exits 0 early when `aws ecr describe-images --repository-name otel-demo-frontend --image-ids imageTag=$TAG` succeeds; logs in with `aws ecr get-login-password --region "$AWS_REGION" | docker login --username AWS --password-stdin "$ECR_REGISTRY"`; runs `docker buildx build --platform "$NODE_PLATFORM" --provenance=false --sbom=false -f src/frontend/Dockerfile -t "$ECR_REPO_URL:$TAG" --push "$DEMO_DIR"`; prints the pushed tag and the next step (`./demo.sh deploy`)

tasks.title: Lifecycle scripts: init, apply, up, down, destroy, status, nightly
tasks.why: Quick stand-up and stand-down is the whole point of the demo; these are the commands a presenter runs before and after a session.

acceptance_criteria.text: scripts/init.sh: runs `need aws tofu docker jq curl git kubectl helm` and, when kubectl or helm is missing, prints `brew install kubectl helm` and exits 1; runs aws_login and prints the caller identity; derives ACCOUNT_ID from `aws sts get-caller-identity --query Account`, creates S3 bucket `otel-demo-eks-tfstate-$ACCOUNT_ID` in $AWS_REGION only if `aws s3api head-bucket` fails, then enables versioning and a public-access block on it; runs `tofu -chdir=tofu init -input=false -backend-config=bucket=... -backend-config=key=otel-demo-eks/terraform.tfstate -backend-config=region=$AWS_REGION`; runs `helm repo add open-telemetry https://open-telemetry.github.io/opentelemetry-helm-charts` (ignoring already-exists) and `helm repo update open-telemetry`; warns (does not fail) when envvars.clickhouse or envvars.aws is missing, naming the .example to copy

scripts/up.sh: aws_login; kubeconfig; NODE_COUNT=$(tf_out node_count); ng_scale "$NODE_COUNT"; wait_nodes_ready "$NODE_COUNT"; then `exec "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/deploy.sh"`. scripts/down.sh [--keep]: tunnel_stop (tolerating no tunnel); unless --keep runs `helm uninstall otel-demo -n otel-demo --ignore-not-found --wait --timeout 5m` then `kubectl delete ns otel-demo clickstack --ignore-not-found --timeout=300s`; finally ng_scale 0; prints a line stating telemetry in ClickHouse Cloud is untouched

scripts/apply.sh [--yes]: aws_login; `tofu -chdir=tofu apply` (with -auto-approve when --yes); kubeconfig; `kubectl get nodes -o wide`; prints `tofu output` and the next steps (./demo.sh build-frontend, ./demo.sh deploy). scripts/destroy.sh [--purge-state]: runs the full down sequence tolerating a missing cluster/release, then `tofu -chdir=tofu destroy`, and with --purge-state empties and deletes the state bucket after tofu destroy succeeds

scripts/status.sh exits 0 whether the node group is at 0 or N and prints: caller identity and account; node group desired size and status; `kubectl get nodes` when desired > 0; pods by phase via `kubectl get pods -A --no-headers -o custom-columns=P:.status.phase | sort | uniq -c`; `helm list -n otel-demo`; tunnel_status result; whether ECR holds the image tag $(frontend_tag); and the scheduler's State, ScheduleExpression and ScheduleExpressionTimezone from `aws scheduler get-schedule --name $(tf_out scheduler_name)`

scripts/nightly.sh on|off reads the existing schedule with `aws scheduler get-schedule`, then calls `aws scheduler update-schedule` re-supplying --schedule-expression, --schedule-expression-timezone, --flexible-time-window and --target from that output with --state ENABLED (on) or DISABLED (off); any other argument prints usage and exits 1

All seven scripts start with a header usage comment and `set -euo pipefail`, source scripts/lib/common.sh, aws.sh and (where kubectl is used) k8s.sh, call aws_login before any AWS command, and pass `bash -n`

security_findings.description: ECR vulnerability scanning is explicitly disabled on the repository holding the custom-built frontend image (Node/Next.js with a patched dependency tree, pullPolicy Always onto nodes with public IPs). security_findings.description: The ClickHouse Cloud password is passed on curl argv three times per run, visible to other local users via ps for up to 60 s per query. The clickstack user has INSERT/CREATE TABLE grants on otel, so leakage lets another local user tamper with the telemetry store. Narrow path (same-host multi-user Mac).
security_findings.remediation: Replace -u with a curl config via process substitution: curl -sS --max-time 60 -K <(printf 'user = "%s:%s"\n' "$CLICKHOUSE_USER" "$CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD") --data-binary @- "${CLICKHOUSE_ENDPOINT}/". Amend task 5 ac2 (pins the literal -u user:pass form).

security_findings.evidence: kubectl -n "$NS_DEMO" create secret generic clickstack-otlp-token --from-literal=OTLP_AUTH_TOKEN="$OTLP_AUTH_TOKEN" --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
security_findings.description: The OTLP shared secret authenticating every request to the ClickStack collector is placed on kubectl argv, visible to any local user via ps while the command runs. The neighbouring clickstack-credentials Secret (deploy.sh:47-48) correctly uses --from-env-file.
security_findings.remediation: Feed the value via stdin: printf '%s' "$OTLP_AUTH_TOKEN" | kubectl -n "$NS_DEMO" create secret generic clickstack-otlp-token --from-file=OTLP_AUTH_TOKEN=/dev/stdin --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -.
